title: CICAN Dublin Archive — Batch 063 NIAH candidate evidence packet

candidates.description_summary: End-of-terrace two-bay two-storey house over raised basement, one of a terrace of four. Double-pile slate roof hipped north; yellow-brick chimneystacks and clay pots; bracketed cast-iron gutters and red-brick sawtooth eaves; brown Flemish-bond brick over granite plinth; gauged-brick voussoirs; replacement casement windows and door; granite platform and steps; wrought-iron railings.
candidates.appraisal_summary: Part of nineteenth-century development of southern Seville Place following arrival of the railway in the 1830s–1840s. NIAH notes the composed terrace and contribution of wrought-iron railings and sawtooth eaves.

candidates.description_summary: Terraced two-bay two-storey brown-brick house, one of a pair. Double-pile pitched slate roof behind parapet with granite coping; brown-brick shouldered chimneystacks; Flemish-bond brick over granite plinth; gauged-brick voussoirs; replacement uPVC windows; moulded segmental-headed entrance; panelled timber door, engaged pilasters, frieze and cornice; granite threshold and front railings.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes this as one of a pair built in the decades after the Dublin and Drogheda railway, retaining much of its original character.

candidates.description_summary: End-of-terrace two-bay two-storey brown-brick house, one of a pair. Double-pile pitched slate roof behind parapet with granite coping; brown-brick shouldered chimneystacks; Flemish-bond brick over granite plinth; altered two-over-two timber sash at first floor and replacement uPVC windows elsewhere; segmental-headed entrance in moulded render surround; replacement door, pilasters, scrolled brackets, frieze and cornice; granite threshold.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes a modestly proportioned house forming one of a pair, built after the Dublin and Drogheda railway; remaining original character contributes to the streetscape.

candidates.description_summary: Attached railway embankment with red-brick parapet wall and pilasters, steel railing to south-east, rendered parapet to north-west, snecked rusticated limestone walls, limestone platband and coping, and segmental-headed blind arcade with gauged yellow-brick voussoirs and rusticated limestone piers; openings blocked.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH notes the functional railway structure is also aesthetically pleasing; yellow-brick voussoirs contrast with rusticated limestone and the structure contributes positively to the streetscape.

candidates.official_title: Saint Laurence O'Toole School, Seville Place, Dublin 1, DUBLIN
candidates.description_summary: Detached three-bay three-storey rendered national school, dated 1936 and designed by Robinson and Keefe. Flat roof behind rendered parapet; continuous lintel and sill courses; red-brick plinth; school crest and date plaque; square-headed windows with replacement uPVC units; vertical strip windows; recessed entrance beneath later metal canopy; projecting external staircase; set within its own grounds with exercise area and boundary walls and railings.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH identifies the modernist design and characteristic flat roof, strong horizontal lines, curved external staircase and white render as significant; it contributes to the architectural variety of the city.
